core_obligations: The bimodule structure and the comparison map (proof lines 5801-5816): the right A-module structure on S comes from the map A to Hom(T, T) composed with the Hom composition; the multiplication then yields the map c_N : N tensor_B S to Hom_B(T, N), functorial in N.

The derived transformation (proof lines 5817-5827): choosing property-(P) and property-(I) replacements P to N to I, the map c_N yields a map P tensor_B S to Hom_B(T, I) between objects representing the derived tensor and the derived Hom, whence a transformation of functors as in the statement.

Reduction to shifts (proof lines 5829-5834): to prove c is an isomorphism assume N has property (P); since T is compact and both sides are exact functors of triangulated categories, lemma-property-P-sequence reduces to N with a finite filtration by sums of B[k], and a second exactness-plus-compactness reduction reaches N = B[k], where assumption (2) says exactly that c is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Give S its bimodule structure through the dg-category composition and build the counit-type map c_N.
Transport c to the derived functors via property-(P) and property-(I) replacements.
Use compactness of T and exactness of both sides to reduce through finite filtrations to shifts of B.
Read the final case off assumption (2).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the derived Hom against a bimodule T satisfying compactness and representability hypotheses with the derived tensor by the dual S (statement lines 5782-5798). The proof (lines 5800-5834) is a genuine adjunction-building argument: the bimodule structure and the counit-type multiplication, the transport to derived functors through property-(P) and property-(I) replacements, and the two-step compactness reduction through finite filtrations down to the shift case where assumption (2) is exactly the claim. H2: the reduction architecture and the way the hypothesis lands on the final case carry the proof.
